cvEn:
Eitan Valenshtein, son of Hava and Itzhak, was born on the 28th of Elul 5725 (25 September 1965) in Ashkelon. Eitan attended the Katzenelson Elementary School in Ashkelon. He continued his studies at the ORT vocational school, in the electronics track, where he studied for one year. He then moved to the Air Force Technical School in Haifa, where he completed his studies as a ground-control electronics technician and obtained his matriculation certificate. When he entered the technical school, Eitan signed a commitment to serve one additional year in the regular army after completing his compulsory service.

Eitan was a member of the model-aircraft club at his school, and of the shooting club of Gadna, the youth battalions. He was very talented, loved graphic design, enjoyed watching films and also making some films himself. Eitan used to say that he would be an amateur filmmaker, and that his profession would be electronics.

In March 1983 Eitan enlisted in the IDF and served in the Air Force. He took several professional courses, among them a course in missile guidance and ground-control systems. During his service at the Air Force base, Eitan sometimes served as the duty driver on the base. In September 1983 he was promoted to Corporal.

On Thursday, 5 Tishrei 5745 (1 October 1984), Eitan was driving a military vehicle, carrying a group of soldiers toward the squadron. His vehicle was involved in a road accident, in which Eitan was killed and seven other soldiers were wounded. He was 19 years old at his death. He was laid to rest in the military cemetery in Ashkelon. He is survived by his parents and two brothers.

The commander of his unit wrote to his family in a letter of condolence: "From the moment he arrived at the base, Eitan proved to be a young man with a heart of gold, always willing to help his comrades as much as was needed. He was loved and respected by all his friends. Eitan performed his role as a computer technician in the Air Force very well and without fault. He was a model soldier, quiet and disciplined. Despite the heavy workload, he always found time to work on improving the appearance of his section, and for this he made use of his skills in graphic design and drawing."
